title: Unit-normalized finite scalar extension and geometric pullback
statement:
Use the canonical coefficient and functor definitions of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion], [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change]. For every prime l, finite extension E of Q_l, scheme morphism j : U → X and positive quotient exponent n+1 (Lean index n), with the canonical internal coefficient rings and derived functors, A finite derived scalar/pullback comparison with the prescribed scalar-unit equation.
Source: Stacks 06YY, 07A6; blueprint integral open direct image, Reduction paragraph
(blueprint: lem-sfb-integral-reduction-pullback-normalization).

Lean statement (under the displayed l, E and j parameters):
theorem integral_reduction_pullback_normalization (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ b :
      (CondensedRing.upperStar (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) j).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
          AdicCompletion.derivedReduction l E U n ≅
        AdicCompletion.derivedReduction l E X n ⋙
          (CondensedRing.upperStar
            (DerivedNakayama.quotientRing l E (n + 1)) j).mapDerivedCategory,
      ∀ M : DerivedCategory (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X),
        (CondensedRing.upperStar (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) j).mapDerivedCategory.map
            ((Mod.derivedExtendMapDerivedCategoryAdjunction
              (AdicCompletion.quotient l E X n)).unit.app M) ≫
          (CondensedRing.derivedComapUpperStarIso
            (DerivedNakayama.reductionRing l E (n + 1)) j).inv.app
              ((AdicCompletion.derivedReduction l E X n).obj M) =
        (Mod.derivedExtendMapDerivedCategoryAdjunction
          (AdicCompletion.quotient l E U n)).unit.app
            ((CondensedRing.upperStar
              (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) j).mapDerivedCategory.obj M) ≫
          (AdicCompletion.restrict l E U n).map (b.hom.app M)

proof.text: Identify each component of integralReductionPullbackMap with FreeParameterEvaluation.scalarPullComparison specialized to integerRing l E, quotientRing l E (n+1), and reductionRing l E (n+1). The quotient coefficientMap is definitionally AdicCompletion.quotient. The identification follows by applying the target scalar adjunction homEquiv injectively and using Mathlib unit_mateEquiv_symm and homEquiv_unit; it identifies the specified transformation, not an unspecified isomorphism.

Apply scalarPullComparison_isIso from def-sfb-free-parameter-scalar-maps to every component. NatIso.isIso_of_isIso_app makes the specified natural transformation invertible. Take b = asIso integralReductionPullbackMap. Its hom is definitionally that inverse mate, so Mathlib unit_mateEquiv_symm proves precisely the required scalar-unit equation for every M. No flatness of reductionRing, boundedness, or geometric hypothesis on j is added.
